newsitem.title: GERMANY: Lufthansa mulls air cargo service-related.
newsitem.headline: Lufthansa mulls air cargo service-related.

text.p: Lufthansa Cargo AG said it was considering dropping common air cargo rates from all German airports in favour of modular service-orientated prices.
Joachim Haas, Lufthansa Cargo senior vice president Europe, said the airline was in talks with forwarders and aimed for a decision by the end of February.
At present, the trucking of air cargo by road from Hamburg to Frankfurt, for example, for an onward flight was effectively free, he told Reuters in an interview.
"A kilo costs just the same from Frankfurt as from Hamburg but it is flown from Frankfurt and the feeder is given away," he said.
"We are thinking about changing the prices so that they fit the service more and the question of common rating is part of that," he said.
The trucking price could be shown in a modular price which would reflect which services a client bought, Haas suggested.
Another option was to accept freight only at the airport of departure, meaning mostly Frankfurt, Cologne and Munich since these had the bulk of intercontinental flights.

Haas explained: "We have looked at our services and seen there are many things where we must really think about taking them out to make everything more transparent and so people can decide what they really want.
"Not only can the client choose what he wants but I think we will go in the direction of looking at the viability of some clients for us," he added.
Most airlines were losing money in cargo at present and did not know which clients were profitable or not for them.
"If I look at our results for 1996, a loss, then I can only come to the conclusion that most shipments and most clients have not earned us any money," Haas said.
"If that is so, then we must seriously see where we earn and where we do not earn, and where we do not earn, then either drop
